## Divider

Rule separating content. Horizontal (default) renders a native `<hr>`; vertical renders a `<div role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical">`, since a native `<hr>` is semantically horizontal-only. Either way it is a semantic separator by default; a caller wanting it purely decorative passes `role="none"` or `aria-hidden` (which also drops `aria-orientation`). Consumes semantic tokens only; the parent layout owns the surrounding spacing, and vertical needs a sized container to fill.

## Indicator

Inline status dot. The root is a `<span role="img">` named by the required `aria-label` (the state, e.g. "Available"), so the state is never colour-only (WCAG 1.4.1); `intent` only tints the dot. A caller whose visible text already states the state passes `aria-hidden` to make it decorative. `pulse` adds a live halo that stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

## LanguageSwitcher

Segmented toggle for the FR/EN locale axis. Reads `locale` and calls `setLocale` on the nearest `OmniaThemeProvider`, so it takes no value props — the provider is the single source of truth. One button per locale, each labelled with its own endonym and `lang`; the active one carries `aria-pressed`. The group root gets a localized accessible name; `className`, `style` and `ref` land on it, and any other native attribute spreads onto it.

Segmented toggle for the light/dark theme axis (not the skin). ## Card

Surface grouping related content, with optional `Card.Header`, `Card.Body` and `Card.Footer` parts composed in source order. Every part is a plain `<div>` with no role of its own: wrap the card in an `<article>` or a list item when its content stands alone. Consumes semantic tokens only, reskins across the theme and skin axes, and steps its padding up with its own width; footer actions wrap on a narrow card.

## DescriptionList

Term–detail pairs on a native `<dl>`. Each `DescriptionList.Item` is a `<div>` group holding one `DescriptionList.Term` (`<dt>`) and its `DescriptionList.Detail` (`<dd>`). Field wrapper that links a label, a description and an error to one control. The control is rendered through `FormField.Control render` or wired with `useFormField()`: atoms never read the field.
